security_audit.summary: I found no evidence of prompt injection, malicious command execution, data exfiltration, or real secrets. The static findings are false positives caused by README prose, Markdown links, template filenames, and placeholder environment variable rows.

remediation.issue: Secret placeholders in the internal README template could be copied too literally.
remediation.suggestion: Add a short note that README files should list variable names only, never secret values or private vault paths.

remediation.issue: Reference examples include parent-directory links that can trigger path-traversal scanners.
remediation.suggestion: Keep the examples, but label them as Markdown documentation links to reduce future audit noise.

content.user_title: Build Better READMEs for Every Project
content.value_statement: README files often miss the needs of their real audience. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code draft, update, and review README content with targeted templates.
actual_capabilities: Selects README sections for open source, personal, internal, and config projects.
Guides creation, additions, updates, and reviews through task-specific questions.
Uses templates for OSS, personal, internal, and XDG config README formats.
Checks for missing install steps, missing examples, stale sections, and generic tone.
References Standard Readme and practical README guidance for deeper structure.
limitations: Needs accurate project context from files or the user before drafting final content.
Does not replace full API documentation, architecture records, or runbooks.
Cannot verify commands, links, or behavior unless the relevant project files are available.
Internal templates need careful editing before publishing sensitive operational details.

use_cases.title: Create an Open Source README
use_cases.description: Draft a contributor-friendly README with install, usage, contributing, and license sections.

use_cases.title: Refresh Internal Service Docs
use_cases.description: Update onboarding, setup, architecture, and troubleshooting sections after a service changes.

use_cases.title: Document a Personal Project
use_cases.description: Create a clear portfolio README that explains purpose, tech stack, usage, and lessons learned.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a Basic README
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a new project README.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a README for this project. Ask me for the audience, project type, setup steps, and main usage before drafting.

prompt_templates.title: Add a Missing Section
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request for improving an existing README.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my README and add a section for [topic]. Place it where it best fits the current structure.

prompt_templates.title: Update Stale Documentation
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request after project behavior changed.
prompt_templates.prompt: Update the README for these changes: [changes]. Flag sections that no longer match the project.

prompt_templates.title: Audit README Against Code
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for a repository-aware documentation review.
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare the README with package metadata, main files, and setup instructions. List accuracy issues, then propose exact edits.

output_examples.input: A maintainer needs a README for a new command line tool.
output_examples.output: A concise README outline with install steps, first-run usage, examples, contribution notes, and license guidance.

output_examples.input: A team service README is missing onboarding details.
output_examples.output: A revised internal README plan covering prerequisites, environment variables, local setup, architecture, runbooks, and troubleshooting.

output_examples.input: A config directory needs documentation for future maintenance.
output_examples.output: A focused README explaining what is stored, why it exists, how to extend it, and known gotchas.

best_practices: Define the audience before choosing README sections.
Include the quickest verified path from install to a useful result.
Review examples and setup steps after meaningful project changes.
anti_patterns: Using an open source template for every project.
Publishing placeholders or secret values in internal README files.
Writing long background sections before basic usage information.

faq.question: What project types does this skill support?
faq.answer: It supports open source, personal, internal, and config-focused README files.

faq.question: Can it update an existing README?
faq.answer: Yes. It can review current content, identify stale sections, and propose focused edits.

faq.question: Does it write full documentation sites?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on README files and can point to deeper documentation when needed.

faq.question: Can it check whether README commands are correct?
faq.answer: It can inspect available project files, but command accuracy depends on the context you provide.

faq.question: Is it useful for private internal projects?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes an internal template for onboarding, architecture, runbooks, and troubleshooting.

faq.question: How does it avoid generic README output?
faq.answer: It asks about audience, project type, task, and the fastest path to a working result.
